Change c0292. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XV.

Context before (unchanged): At first his countenance was illuminated with pleasure, but, as he continued, thoughtfulness and sadness succeeded; at length, laying aside the instrument, he sat absorbed in reflection.

1818 text: "My heart beat quick; this was the hour and moment of trial, which would decide my hopes, or realize my fears.

1831 text: "My heart beat quick; this was the hour and moment of trial, which would decide my hopes, or realise my fears.

Diff: " My heart beat quick; this was the hour and moment of trial, which would decide my hopes, or [-realize-] {+realise+} my fears.

result.rationale: Only orthographic variation: 'realize' (1818) becomes 'realise' (1831). The word, meaning, and syntax are identical, so there is no interpretive consequence.
